notes: PvPad targets Ethereum Sepolia (11155111). Manifest regenerated against the post-review revision (CHANGELOG.md, 'Revision after independent review'); contract identifiers and constructor arguments are unchanged, the hook and factory creation bytes are not. Both PoolManager constructor arguments use Uniswap's Sepolia deployment listed at https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4/deployments#sepolia-11155111; target-chain simulation must verify the external dependency. LaunchToken is the protocol launch artifact, distinct from the identically named Pepe Values Pepe / PVP genesis PvPadToken. The pool object describes the protocol LaunchToken pool; admission fee 3000 is not a claim about its effective trading fee. PvPadFactory creates its own FeeEscrow and zero-create-fee genesis token and BondingCurve during construction; later createLaunch calls create additional token/curve pairs. These children require no separate manifest entries or initialization calls. Pad pools use native ETH, fee tier 0, tick spacing 60 and the factory's canonical graduation price. Pad trades charge 1%, split between king and creator; graduation at 4.2 ETH locks factory-owned liquidity. Launch fees and king bids fund WorkerSubsidy. Revision behaviour: PvPadHook.realignPool(key, target), callable only by a pool's bound registry, moves an initialized, liquidity-free pool to the canonical price with a zero-value swap; when all 16 bounded salt candidates are preinitialized at a foreign price the factory (including the genesis launch in its constructor) uses the first candidate, realigns it, re-checks the price and emits LaunchPoolRealigned, so poisoning no longer blocks factory deployment or createLaunch. PvPadFactory.receive() reverts NotBondingCurve for anything but a registered curve's graduation sweep, and BondingCurve has no receive(). WorkerSubsidy.setEpoch rejects a window that starts or lasts more than 90 days ahead. PvPadHook has only the PoolManager constructor argument and requires CREATE2 address bits (address & 0x3fff) == 0x08cc (beforeAddLiquidity, beforeSwap, afterSwap, both swap return deltas, no beforeInitialize). Deployment must supply a salt mined for the actual deployer, the attested creation code and the encoded PoolManager argument; this schema has no salt field and these notes do not configure one. The hook creation code changed in this revision, so every salt mined for earlier creation code, including the reviewer's, is void; script/MineHookSalt.s.sol --sig mine(address,address) prints the init-code hash, salt and predicted address offline. PvPadFactory construction immediately binds and initializes or realigns genesis through that hook and PoolManager, so the protected deployment floor, admission and gas estimation must run against Sepolia state with PoolManager code at the configured address; the four application constructors plus LaunchToken measured about 12.8M gas locally, the factory alone about 8.8M. Policy-resolved $owner is used for both the worker epoch updater and genesis creator fee beneficiary; these are separate roles whose assignment to the same address requires policy authorization and review. The updater controls Merkle allocations; genesis creator fees cannot be reassigned. Any contract can bind its own pool to the shared hook; identify launches only through PvPadFactory. The protocol factory supplies MerkleDistributor and PoolInitializationGuard. Policy, signed artifact linkage, independent review, admission, deployment and publication remain service responsibilities; this manifest does not assert those outcomes.
